text: Git branching is a powerful feature of version control that helps developers work together without interfering with each other’s code. In a typical workflow, each developer creates a separate feature branch from the main branch to build a new function or fix a bug. This keeps the main code stable while the work is in progress. Once the feature is complete, the developer submits a pull request, which invites teammates to review the changes and discuss any improvements. After the review is approved, the branch is merged back into the main branch. This structured process reduces conflicts and ensures that every change is checked before becoming part of the project.
